case_title: Nara Chandrababu Naidu v. The State of Andhra Pradesh & Anr.
accused_occupation: Former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh (alleged offences committed while in office, 2015-2019)
evidence_type: Documentary (official letters, GST and tax authority material, forensic audit, Anti-Corruption Bureau correspondence); no trial evidence assessed
trial_court_outcome: Special Judge remanded the accused to judicial custody on 10.09.2023 (no verdict; pre-trial remand)
high_court_outcome: Petition seeking quashing of FIR and remand order dismissed
neutral_facts: A first information report was lodged in December 2021 with a state police station, initially naming twenty-six persons, concerning funds meant for a state skill development project. The allegation was that about Rs.370 crore of government money set aside for six skill development clusters was diverted. Investigators alleged that a corporate partner's contribution was not made and that the state's outflow of funds went to a private company. They alleged that a related company, which had been paid for software supplies, sourced those supplies from companies that were shell or defunct entities providing no services and that issued invoices without supplying services. A tax authority examining cenvat credit claims had earlier found that work had been sub-contracted without contractual provision. A forensic audit in 2020 reported irregularities in use of funds for 2014-2015 to 2018-2019. It was alleged that the project was allotted on nomination without tender, that officials were appointed without cabinet approval, and that the accused, who held senior elected office in the state government during 2015 to 2019, approved cost estimates and pursued release of funds. It was further alleged that a project note file was removed from the secretariat to conceal the offences.
number_of_offences: 12 charged (10 IPC sections plus PC Act ss.12 and 13, with ss.120-B, 34, 37 as ancillary); 0 finally upheld
financial_property_loss: Approximately Rs.370 crore of government funds allegedly diverted (allegation, not a court finding)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court; prior conspiracy alleged by the State
motive: alleged: misappropriation of government funds through corrupt and illegal methods
key_evidence_accepted: Documentary record (ACB letters of 05.06.2018, 22.02.2021 and later) relied on only to hold that no enquiry commenced before s.17A; no merits evidence accepted
post_offence_conduct: alleged by the State: project note file removed from secretariat to tamper with evidence (not decided by the court)
custody_duration: Arrested 09.09.2023 and remanded to judicial custody from 10.09.2023; total duration not stated
bail_history: Enlarged on bail (date and grant order not stated)
trial_duration: offence: 2015-2019 (alleged); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 22.09.2023; Supreme Court: 16 January 2024
legal_representation: Appellant: Harish N. Salve, Sidharth Luthra and other advocates; State: P. Sudhakar Reddy (A.A.G.), Mukul Rohatgi, Ranjit Kumar and other advocates
investigation_status: FIR registered 09.12.2021; accused added 08.09.2023; arrested 09.09.2023; investigation ongoing; no charge sheet mentioned
procedural_irregularity: No prior approval under s.17A obtained before action against the accused under the PC Act (Bose J held the action under the 1988 Act illegal); Trivedi J held s.17A not applicable to pre-2018 offences
appeal_history: Trial court (Special Judge): remand order 10.09.2023 upheld by Bose J as within jurisdiction; High Court: quashing petition dismissed 22.09.2023; Supreme Court: split opinion (Bose J partly allowed; Trivedi J dismissed), referred to larger bench
prosecution_argument: Enquiry began 05.06.2018 before s.17A, so no approval needed; s.17A is substantive and prospective; offences were not in discharge of official duty; IPC offences survive; the Special Court had jurisdiction under ss.3-4 PC Act
defence_argument: Absence of s.17A approval vitiates the investigation, arrest and remand; IPC offences cannot survive since basic material is same; once PC Act offences fall, the Special Court's remand is without jurisdiction and non-est
legal_principle_applied: s.17A requires prior approval for enquiry/investigation of PC Act offences by public servants after it became operational; s.17A is prospective and substantive; remand and IPC offences survive; Section 4(3) and s.223 CrPC principles on joint trial
precedent_relied_upon: Yashwant Sinha (2020) 2 SCC 338; State of Telangana v. Managipet (2019) 19 SCC 87; State of Rajasthan v. Tejmal Choudhary (2021 SCC OnLine SC 3477); Ebha Arjun Jadeja (2019) 9 SCC 789; State through CBI v. Jitender Kumar Singh (2014) 11 SCC 724; M.C. Gupta v. CBI (2012) 8 SCC 669; Vineeta Sharma (2020) 9 SCC 1
other_sentence_order: Liberty to State to seek s.17A approval (Bose J); matter referred to Chief Justice of India for constitution of a larger bench
